{{Short description|American marine biologist}}
'''Sherry Anne Reed''' (February 2, 1959 – December 16, 2019) was an American [[marine biologist]]. She served at the [[Smithsonian Marine Station at Fort Pierce|Smithsonian Marine Station at Link Port]] for over 36 years as a research specialist, station manager, and [[Diving safety|dive safety]] officer.<ref name="Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History">{{Cite web |title=In Memoriam: Sherry Anne Reed, 'the heart of SMS' |url=http://naturalhistory.si.edu/research/smithsonian-marine-station/news/memoriam-sherry-anne-reed-heart-sms |access-date=2022-11-17 |website=Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History |language=en}}</ref> Reed is known as the first female scientific diving officer in the United States.<ref name="Women Divers Hall of Fame">{{Cite web |title=2002 Sherry Reed |url=https://www.wdhof.org/members/sherry-reed |access-date=2022-11-17 |website=Women Divers Hall of Fame}}</ref>

== Early life ==
Reed was born in 1959 in [[Bourne, Massachusetts|Bourne]], [[Cape Cod|Cape Cod, Massachusetts]].<ref name="TC Palm-2019"/> She attended [[Wheaton College (Massachusetts)|Wheaton College]] in Massachusetts, where she studied marine science.<ref name="TC Palm-2019">{{Cite web |date=2019-12-31 |title=Sherry Anne Reed |url=https://tcpalm.com/obituaries/tcn013750 |access-date=2022-11-17 |website=TC Palm |language=en}}</ref>

In 1982, Reed graduated from [[Wheaton College (Massachusetts)|Wheaton College]] in [[Massachusetts]] with a bachelor's degree in [[biology]] and started her first marine science career at the [[National Museum of Natural History|Smithsonian Museum of Natural History]], where she assisted with curating the octopus and [[Mollusca|mollusk]] collections.<ref name="Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History" />

== Professional career ==
In 1983, Reed joined the [[Smithsonian Marine Station at Fort Pierce|Smithsonian Marine Station at Link Port]] in Florida as a marine biological research assistant.<ref name="TC Palm-2019" /> During her studies of the local marine organisms and ecosystem, two new marine species were found and named after her—''Smithsoniarhynches sherryreedae'', a new species of [[flatworm]] found in [[Indian River Lagoon]],<ref name="Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Smithsoniarhynches Sherryreedae |url=https://collections.si.edu/search/detail/edanmdm:nmnhinvertebratezoology_817247?q=Smithsoniarhynches+sherryreedae&record=1&hlterm=Smithsoniarhynches%2Bsherryreedae |website=Smithsonian Institution}}</ref> and ''Celleporaria sherryae'', a new species of [[bryozoa]]n found in the [[Gulf of Mexico]].<ref name="Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Celleporaria sherryae Winston, 2005 |url=https://www.marinespecies.org/aphia.php?p=taxdetails&id=422328 |access-date=2022-11-17 |website=WoRMS – World Register of Marine Species}}</ref>

Reed also served for many years as a dive safety officer for the [[Smithsonian Marine Station at Fort Pierce|Smithsonian Marine Station]] and the Caribbean Coral Research Ecosystem Program until she was promoted to station manager in 2015.<ref name="Women Divers Hall of Fame" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Sherry Reed {{!}} Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History |url=http://naturalhistory.si.edu/staff/sherry-reed |access-date=2022-11-17 |website=naturalhistory.si.edu |language=en}}</ref> She had supervised thousands of scientific research dives throughout [[Florida]], [[Belize]] and the [[Caribbean]].<ref name="Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History" /> Over the years, she saved a dozen people and various animals from drowning, and a FPL lineman from electrocution.<ref name="Yates Funeral Home">{{Cite web |title=Sherry Anne Reed Obituary |url=https://www.yatesfuneralhome.com/obituaries/obituary-listings?obId=13996156 |access-date=2022-11-17 |website=Yates Funeral Home |language=en-US}}</ref> Besides a passionate scientific diver and officer, Reed was a licensed [[United States Coast Guard Charter Boat Captain's license|Coast Guard captain]] and a certified instructor of [[PADI|PADI scuba]], [[Cardiopulmonary resuscitation|CPR]], [[first aid]], and [[accident management]].<ref name="Yates Funeral Home" />

Reed was a member of various professional organizations. She served on the Smithsonian's Diving Control Board and the Board of Directors of both the [[American Academy of Underwater Sciences]].<ref name="Women Divers Hall of Fame" /> She became part of the Board of Directors of the [[Women Divers Hall of Fame|Women Divers Hall of Fame (WDHOF)]] in 2002<ref name="Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History" /> and served as the secretary (2006–2011) and the vice-president (2011–2014).<ref name="Women Divers Hall of Fame" />
